newsitem.title: CHINA: China province Jan-Sept exports down 0.8 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China province Jan-Sept exports down 0.8 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's southern province of Guangdong exported $41.22 billion worth of goods in January to September, a drop of 0.8 percent compared with the same period of 1995, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
Imports edged up 2.4 percent to $34.9 billion, the newspaper quoted customs figures as showing.
Guangdong has been at the forefront of China's economic reform and is a mainstay of the country's light industrial and manufactured goods production.
The province had a record trade surplus of $6.32 billion during the period. Its foreign trade accounted for 38.1 percent of China's total, the newspaper said.
In the first six months of this year, Guangdong's exports fell 7.4 percent and imports rose two percent, official data show.
"The export decrease has been controlled, but the outlook is not too optimistic," the newspaper quoted a provincial customs official as saying. The official did not elaborate.
Traditional exports such as textiles, garments and light industrial products continued to be Guangdong's major foreign currency earners, the newspaper said.
Exports of textiles and garments were $4.83 billion during the nine-month period, those of shoes were $2.65 billion and toys, $2.0 billion, it said.

Nearly 36 percent of exports, or $14.81 billion worth, were to neighbouring Hong Kong while exports to the United States totalled $9.61 billion. Exports to the European Union were $5.06 billion and those to Japan were $4.89 billion, it said.
Raw materials dominated imports, it said. The province imported $3.2 billion of plastics, $2.07 billion of steel, $1.3 billion in electronics and $1.07 billion in paper and paper board, it said.
